cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make the Second Step First
cards.instruction: Get them to accept a small consequence that makes the larger risky action feel already underway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put down the climbing-course deposit. We can discuss the cliff after we've secured the places.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't agreed to climb. Is the deposit refundable?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if we attend the first lesson. Book us both; I'll make sure we're there to ask for it back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So once I've paid, you can use getting my money back to get me to the lesson.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Put your name down first, then mine. Tomorrow I'll pick you up for the refund, and we can meet the instructor while we're waiting.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders payment before cliff discussion; A3 interprets refund question as a route to attendance; A5 directs registration and pickup so the small payment advances the risky plan.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2 refund question explicitly; A5 adopts B4 description of the trap and turns it into a concrete lesson trip.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks a practical financial safeguard and B4 accurately identifies how A would exploit it, plausible reluctance.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 refund motive to arrange getting to the instructor while still calling the journey refund retrieval.

specificity.evidence: A1 climbing course and A3 attendance condition establish the consequence; A5 pickup is a proposed plan rather than completed travel.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 words for the refund maintain the live pretext; long enough to include actual next actions.
